## What the context pass changed

Two corrections the plan has to absorb:

1. **The margin is mechanically bounded at 3,000 B — so neither of the body's
   first two options can change the class.** Acceptance item 1 asks for "a
   stated, deliberate margin below its cap (either by slimming or by a recorded
   cap decision)". The loose-cap hygiene arm FAILs any cap more than 3,000 B
   above live size, so: raising the cap can never buy more than 3,000 B of
   headroom, and slimming can buy at most 3,000 - 813 = 2,187 B of additional
   margin before the same arm forces a ratchet-down. Against the body's own
   measured growth rate (3,219 B in one ~5-hour window, four independent
   landings), even the mechanical MAXIMUM margin is under one day. Option 1
   (slim) and option 2 (raise the cap) are therefore both instance fixes with a
   sub-day half-life, by construction. Only option 3 — changing the ratchet's
   failure attribution — can address the class.

2. **The "fleet-wide" collateral is real but narrower than stated.** The body
   says "every OTHER session's Step 9c gate goes red on a condition none of them
   introduced". Step 9c's known-red stripping is node-level, so a session whose
   branch does NOT touch SKILL.md sees the same failing node in both its own run
   and the pristine baseline and has it stripped; and the no-flags run is not a
   pre-commit hook, so commits are not blocked either. The verified failure modes
   are instead:
   (a) **Self-blocking, and this is the dominant one:** a branch that grows
       SKILL.md past its cap fails its OWN Step 9c gate, discovered late (after
       the full implementation round) and expensively — `test_workflow_lint.py`
       alone is the gate's long pole (median ~13 min, max ~30 min, 4,950 s
       derived budget).
   (b) **The moving-main class:** a sibling lands a SKILL.md edit and raises the
       cap; a concurrent branch that then merges main exceeds the NEW cap and
       must re-measure. The cap ladder's own comments call this "the norm, not the
       exception" and already prescribe the mitigation ("re-measure at Step 10d,
       never at Step 4").

Neither correction reduces the task's urgency — 813 B of headroom on the repo's
most-edited file is a real trip-wire — but they do move the target from "buy
margin" to "make the trip-wire cheap to hit". The planner should price all three
options against (1) and (2) rather than against the body's original framing, and
should treat the `adversarial-planner/SKILL.md` sibling (521 B) as the same
instance, not a separate class.

Self-referential note for the planner: any slimming option edits the very file
this session is executing from, so the Step 5a family-atomic spec-freshness sync
will see the `workflow` family dirty and skip it. That is expected, not a defect.
